### periodicPlateOptiParam2d

Identification of the two amplitudes of a body force field on a periodic plate,
with the gradient computed by the discrete adjoint lattice Boltzmann method (ALBM).
The inverse problem, the primal setup and the optimizer settings are identical to
`periodicPlateOptiAD2d`; only the way the gradient is obtained differs. Running both
cases on the same grid is therefore a verification of the automatically generated
adjoint collision kernel, since the two methods share nothing but the primal
solution.

The benchmark and its results are described in
[@grafenBenchmarkCasesGradientbased2026].

#### Setup

The domain is the unit square $\Omega = [0,1]^2$ with periodic boundaries,
discretized by $N_x$ nodes per Cartesian direction, and the primal problem is the
quasistationary MRT scheme of [@boolakee:23a] on a `D2Q8` descriptor, in its OpenLB
implementation [@kaiser:25]. The
manufactured displacement

$$
\symbf{u}^*(\symbf{x}) = \begin{pmatrix}
  \delta_1 \cos(2\pi x_1) \sin(2\pi x_2) \\
  \delta_2 \sin(2\pi x_1) \cos(2\pi x_2)
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \delta_1 = 9 \cdot 10^{-4}, \quad \delta_2 = 7 \cdot 10^{-4},
$$

with $E = 0.11$ and $\nu = 0.8$, is produced by the body force

$$
\symbf{F}^* = 4\pi^2 \begin{pmatrix}
  \big[K(\delta_1+\delta_2) + 2\mu\delta_1\big]\cos(2\pi x_1)\sin(2\pi x_2) \\
  \big[K(\delta_1+\delta_2) + 2\mu\delta_2\big]\sin(2\pi x_1)\cos(2\pi x_2)
\end{pmatrix} .
$$

The control scales its two components,
$\symbf{F}(\symbf{x}_n, \symbf{\alpha}) = \symbf{\alpha} \circ \symbf{F}^*(\symbf{x}_n)$, so that
$\symbf{\alpha}^* = (1,1)^{\mathsf{T}}$, and the objective is the squared $L^2$ distance
of the displacement from the sampled target over the whole lattice.

#### Implementation

The case is assembled as an

```cpp
OptiCaseAdjoint<Controlled, MyCase, Adjoint, MyCase, Reference, MyCase,
                Optimality, PeriodicPlate>
```

so the primal and the adjoint problem run on the same lattice type and the
`Optimality` policy evaluates

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}J}{\mathrm{d}\symbf{\alpha}}
  = \Big(\frac{\partial \symbf{g}}{\partial \symbf{\alpha}}\Big)^{\!\mathsf{T}} \symbf{\phi} ,
$$

with the adjoint state $\symbf{\phi}$. The control enters the scheme only through the
forcing, so $\partial \symbf{g}/\partial \symbf{\alpha}$ is a constant conversion factor and
the gradient is proportional to the adjoint displacement.

The control is applied cell-wise through the `opti::CONTROL_VECTOR` field, which the
`StationaryLinearElasticityMRT` collision multiplies component-wise onto
`descriptors::FORCE`. The adjoint of that collision is generated by the CSE codegen
pipeline, so the dual kernel follows any change of the forward collision
automatically; regenerate it with `script/codegen/cse/optimize_dynamics.sh` if the
collision is modified.

The adjoint solve has its own steady-state tolerance, `CONVERGENCE_PRECISION_ADJOINT`.
Setting `SET_ADJOINT_MAX_IT` makes the adjoint run for the same number of pseudo-time
steps as the preceding primal solve instead of using that tolerance.

#### Files

```
periodicPlateOptiParam2d/
├── periodicPlateOptiParam2d.cpp  main(): default parameters, optimizer settings, run
├── case.h                        Case and OptiCase types, geometry, lattice, objective
├── analyticalSolution.h          manufactured displacement, stress and body force
└── Makefile
```

This example ships no case file: the whole study is driven from the command line.
Every parameter set in the `.cpp` can be overridden there (`--RESOLUTION 20`), and
a `--case-file` of the same shape as the ones in `periodicPlateOpti2d` would work
if a study needs its settings pinned. The precedence is
`set<>()` < case file < command line.

The defaults already match the benchmark, including `PHYS_MAX_T 100`,
`ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE true` and both steady-state tolerances at `1e-7`, so only
`--RESOLUTION` has to be varied across the study.

#### Parameters

All of the following are set in `periodicPlateOptiParam2d.cpp` and can be
overridden from a case file or the command line. Vector-valued entries are passed
in brackets, `--INITIAL_CONTROL "[-1 -1]"`.

##### Geometry and discretization

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | int | `40` | nodes per Cartesian direction, $N_x$; the lattice holds $N_x^2$ nodes |
| `DOMAIN_EXTENT` | double[2] | `{1.0, 1.0}` | physical size of the periodic square |
| `ORIGIN` | double[2] | `{0.0, 0.0}` | lower-left corner of the domain |
| `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` | double | `1.0` | characteristic length of the unit converter |
| `PHYS_DELTA_X` | double | derived | $\Delta x =$ `DOMAIN_EXTENT[0] / RESOLUTION` |
| `PHYS_DELTA_T` | double | derived | $\Delta t = \Delta x^2$, the diffusive scaling of the pseudo-time |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DISPLACEMENT` | double | derived | displacement scale of the converter, set to $\Delta x$ |

The three derived values are computed in `main()` from `DOMAIN_EXTENT` and
`RESOLUTION` once the parameter block has been read, so overriding `RESOLUTION`
on the command line updates them too.

##### Material

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOLID_CASE` | string | `"continua"` | dimensional reduction of the constitutive law; accepts `continua`, `planeStress`, `planeStrain` and `standard` |
| `YOUNGS_MODULUS` | double | `0.11` | $E$ of the simulated material |
| `POISSON_RATIO` | double | `0.8` | $\nu$; in 2D the admissible range is $-1 < \nu < 1$ |
| `PHYS_DENSITY` | double | `1` | $\rho$ |
| `DAMPING_FACTOR` | double | `1.0` | $\kappa$ of the damped pseudo-time scheme; also sets the stress conversion factor $\kappa \Delta x^2 / \Delta t$ |

##### Pseudo-time stepping and convergence

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | double | `100` | pseudo-time budget; the step cap is `PHYS_MAX_T`$/\Delta t = $ `PHYS_MAX_T`$\cdot N_x^2$ |
| `CONVERGENCE_PRECISION` | double | `1e-7` | relative tolerance of the primal steady-state check; `0` disables the check and runs the full budget |
| `CONVERGENCE_PRECISION_ADJOINT` | double | `1e-7` | the same tolerance for the adjoint solve |
| `CONV_ITER` | double | `10` | window length of the `ValueTracer` that watches the monitored value |
| `CONV_VALUE` | double | `1` | slot the case writes the monitored value into (the mean squared displacement); not a user knob |
| `CONVERGED_IT` | size_t | `0` | slot holding the step at which the primal solve converged; read back when `SET_ADJOINT_MAX_IT` is set |
| `SET_ADJOINT_MAX_IT` | bool | `false` | `true` runs the adjoint for exactly `CONVERGED_IT` steps instead of applying its own tolerance |

##### Inverse problem and control

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INITIAL_CONTROL` | double[2] | `{-1.0, -1.0}` | $\symbf{\alpha}^{(0)}$, the two scalars scaling the components of $\symbf{F}^*$ |
| `ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE` | bool | `true` | `true` compares against the sampled manufactured displacement, `false` against a reference obtained from a simulation |

##### Output

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VTK_ENABLED` | bool | `true` | write the displacement, stress and control fields to VTK |
| `LATTICE_VTK_ITER_T` | int | `1000` | pseudo-time steps between VTK writes |
| `LATTICE_LOG_ITER_T` | int | `1000` | pseudo-time steps between console log lines; a very large value silences the log |

##### Optimizer

Held in a separate `OptimizerParametersD` in `main()` rather than in the case
parameters, and namespaced by optimizer component.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `optimizer::EPS` | double | `1e-10` | termination tolerance on the gradient norm |
| `optimizer::MAX_OPTIMIZATION_STEPS` | int | `50` | cap on the number of optimization steps |
| `optimizer::VERBOSE` | bool | `true` | per-step optimizer log |
| `linesearch::MAX_STEP_ATTEMPTS` | int | `100` | cap on line-search refinements within one step |
| `linesearch::STEP_CONDITION` | string | `"StrongWolfe"` | acceptance condition of the line search |
| `LBFGS::HISTORY_SIZE` | int | `20` | number of stored vector pairs of the limited-memory inverse Hessian approximation |

#### Running the case

This example has a single mode: there is no `FORWARD_ONLY` switch and no gradient
comparison, so every run solves the inverse problem.

The defaults run $N_x = 40$ from $\symbf{\alpha}^{(0)} = (-1,-1)^{\mathsf{T}}$ with
$T_{max} = 100$. The resolution study of the benchmark uses

```sh
mpirun -np 2 ./periodicPlateOptiParam2d --RESOLUTION 20 --INITIAL_CONTROL "[-1 -1]" \
  --ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE 1 --CONVERGENCE_PRECISION 1e-7 \
  --CONVERGENCE_PRECISION_ADJOINT 1e-7 --PHYS_MAX_T 100 --VTK_ENABLED 0
```

repeated for $N_x \in \{10, 20, 40, 80\}$, writing one row per optimization step to
`tmp/gnuplotData/data/optiLog.dat`.

#### Results

The results of this benchmark are reported and discussed in
[@grafenBenchmarkCasesGradientbased2026]: the evolution of the objective, of the
gradient norm and of the relative control error over the resolutions, and the
agreement between the ALBM gradient computed here and the f-AD gradient of
`periodicPlateOptiAD2d`.
